# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS | **Section:** Aseneth's Beauty and Status

---

**1:1** And it came-to-pass in the first year of the seven years of plenty, in the second month, on the fifth of the month, that Pharaoh sent-forth Joseph to go-about through all the land of Egypt.

**1:2** And Joseph came into the region of Heliopolis, and he was gathering-in the grain of that region as the sand of the sea.

**1:3** And there was a man in that city, a priest of Heliopolis, and his name was Pentephres, and he was a satrap of Pharaoh and his chief-officer, and a great and powerful man in all the land of Egypt.

**1:4** And Pentephres had a virgin daughter, eighteen years of age, tall and beautiful and graceful, excelling all the virgins of the earth, and she bore no resemblance to the virgins of the Egyptians, but was in all respects like the daughters of the Hebrews.

**1:5** And she was tall like Sarah, and beautiful like Rebecca, and graceful like Rachel.

**1:6** And the name of the virgin was Aseneth.

**1:7** And the report of her beauty spread-abroad into all that land and to the ends of the inhabited-world, and all the sons of the rulers and all the sons of the satraps and all the sons of the kings, young-men and mighty-men, sought her as a wife.

**1:8** And there was great strife among them on account of Aseneth, and they were seeking to fight against one another because of her.

**1:9** And the first-born son of Pharaoh also heard concerning her, and he was entreating his father to give her to him as a wife.

**1:10** And he said to him: "Give me Aseneth the daughter of Pentephres the priest of Heliopolis as a wife."

**1:11** And his father Pharaoh said to him: "Why do you seek a wife who is beneath you? Are you not king and ruler over all the land of Egypt? No — behold, the daughter of the king of Moab is betrothed to you, and she herself is a queen. Take her as your wife."

**1:12** And Aseneth despised all men and held them in contempt, and no man had ever seen her, for Pentephres had built adjoining his house a great tower, exceedingly high.

**1:13** And the upper storey of that tower had ten chambers. And the first chamber was large and beautiful, paved with purple stone, and its walls were lined with precious and many-colored stones, and the ceiling of that chamber was of gold.

**1:14** And within it were fixed gods of Egypt without number, of gold and silver, and Aseneth worshiped them all and feared them and made-sacrifice to them each day.

**1:15** The second chamber held all the adornments of Aseneth, and in it were her seven virgin attendants, born on the same night as she, and she loved them greatly.

**1:16** The third chamber held all the good things of Aseneth — much gold and silver, garments woven with gold, and choice stones of great value, and fine linen.

**1:17** And the remaining seven chambers belonged to the seven virgins, one chamber for each.

**1:18** And a stairway of stone led from the ground up to the topmost chamber, having thirty-two steps.

**1:19** And the windows of the upper chamber looked toward the east and toward the south; there were also windows toward the north for the cooling-wind.

---
*EMET: hyphenated compounds preserve Greek constructs; chapter:verse format throughout.*
